messages:
Marta: Quick sync — proposing final contract for the new embeddings endpoint. Need decisions on: batching limits, dims, model choices, response shape, launch criteria. TL;DR: /v1/embeddings accepts inputs: [string], model param, optional metadata[]. Can we finalize today? :hourglass:

Arjun: Platform constraints: we can accept array inputs. Recommended soft limit: 512 items per request for hosted. Large dims (2048) push the practical batch cap down to ~128 on current GPU configs. Dedicated pools can support higher. We should add an async bulk ingestion path for >1k jobs.

Emily: ML tradeoffs: emb-3-small = fastest/cheapest, emb-4-large = best recall. Suggest default model=emb-3-medium (1536 dims) for GA to balance cost/quality. Expose model param so enterprise customers can pick emb-4. Also recommend optional L2-normalize output (query-side opt-in) to avoid surprising users.

Ben: Product asks: Launch criteria -> p95 latency <= 250ms for batches <=16 on hosted; correctness/regression tests with our eval prompts; SDK examples; migration guide. Cost target: ballpark <$0.40 per 1k vectors (we'll refine). Also require idempotency (client-provided id) and stable ordering in responses.

Olga: CS note: multiple enterprise customers requested bulk indexing >1000 items. They want progress reporting and resumable jobs. Propose a job-based async API (POST /v1/embeddings:bulk) returning job_id + status endpoint. Also clarify metadata size limit (e.g., 4KB) and redaction/PII guidance.

Arjun: +1 on job-based async. Implementation notes: add header X-Redwood-Client-Batch-Id for dedupe; server should accept streamed NDJSON for very large uploads. Need to decide backpressure behavior and retry semantics. Also flag: caching layer will need per-customer keys to avoid cross-tenant leakage.

Marta: Proposed synchronous request example and response shape (for spec):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "emb-3-medium",
  "inputs": ["text1", "text2"],
  "metadata": [{"id":"doc1"},{"id":"doc2"}]
}

200 OK
{
  "data": [
    {"id":"doc1","input":"text1","embedding":[0.001,-0.12,...],"meta":{"source":"upload"}},
    {"id":"doc2","input":"text2","embedding":[0.02,0.5,...],"meta":{}}
  ],
  "model": "emb-3-medium",
  "usage": {"vectors": 2}
}
```
Note: prefer field name `embedding` (not `vector`) to match other APIs. Include model_version and quantization tag when applicable.

Emily: Also add `model_version` and `quantization` fields in response (e.g., "model_version":"2026-01-15", "quantization":"q4_0"), so customers can debug embedding drift/regressions. Suggest including a checksum for normalization verification.

Ben: Prioritization proposal: GA scope = synchronous endpoint supporting array inputs, default model emb-3-medium (1536), hosted max batch 512 with p95 SLOs, async bulk ingest as beta. Enterprise scope: emb-4-large (2048 dims), higher batch sizes, dedicated SLOs, long-retention logs. Any objections?

Olga: Ok from CS side — async bulk solves the immediate asks.

Arjun: No engineering objections. I'll open infra tickets: batch-size perf matrix, memory/throughput tests for 1536 vs 2048 dims, and NDJSON streaming prototype.

Marta: I'll convert this thread into a spec doc + launch checklist (perf targets, SDK tasks, docs, analytics). Thanks team! :sparkles:
